title: Masters in Germany Without IELTS — The Complete 2026 Guide for Indian Students
excerpt: A comprehensive 2026 guide for international students who want to pursue a master’s in Germany without IELTS, including universities that accept MOI, visa implications, and career prospects.
content:
Many students believe that IELTS or TOEFL is compulsory for pursuing a master's degree in Germany. However, in 2026, this is no longer always true. Several German public universities accept a Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate as proof of English proficiency.

If your previous education was taught entirely in English, you may be eligible to apply without IELTS or TOEFL, saving time, money, and effort.

What Is MOI (Medium of Instruction)?

MOI is an official certificate issued by your previous university stating that your Bachelor's degree was taught completely in English.

Many German universities consider this certificate sufficient proof of English proficiency, especially for applicants from countries like India.

Can You Apply for Masters in Germany Without IELTS?

Yes, you can apply for a master's degree in Germany without IELTS if the university explicitly accepts MOI as a language requirement.

Each university and program sets its own criteria. Some accept MOI directly, while others may accept it conditionally or alongside additional documents.

Public Universities Accepting MOI as Language Proof

Below are some well-known German public universities that have accepted MOI for selected master's programs in previous intakes:

  • Technical University of Darmstadt (TU Darmstadt)
  • University of Freiburg
  • Free University of Berlin
  • Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen-Nuremberg (FAU)
  • University of Siegen
  • University of Kiel
  • University of Kassel
  • Kempten University of Applied Sciences
  • And many more (program-specific)

Acceptance of MOI depends heavily on your academic background, chosen course, and intake year.

What Can You Submit Instead of IELTS for Masters in Germany?

German universities that waive IELTS typically accept the following alternatives:

  • Medium of Instruction Certificate — a letter from your undergraduate university confirming your degree was taught in English. This is the most commonly accepted alternative for Indian students from English-medium universities.
  • Duolingo English Test (DET) — accepted by a growing number of German universities. Score requirements vary (typically 110–120).
  • TestDaF or Goethe Certificate — if you are applying to a German-taught program, B2 or C1 German language certification replaces English proficiency requirements entirely.
  • TOEFL — most German universities that accept IELTS also accept TOEFL. Minimum scores are typically 90+ (iBT).
  • GRE with English Proficiency — some programs use your GRE verbal score as a proxy for English ability.

Step-by-Step: How to Apply for Masters in Germany Without IELTS

  1. Identify programs that specifically waive IELTS for graduates of English-medium undergraduate programs.
  2. Obtain a Medium of Instruction (MOI) certificate from your undergraduate college or university, usually from the registrar's office.
  3. Check each university's English proficiency requirements on its official admissions page, because waiver conditions differ by program.
  4. Prepare your APS certificate. It is mandatory for Indian students whether or not IELTS is waived.
  5. Write your SOP and collect your LORs, tailored to each program. Our SOP writing for German universities service can help.
  6. Apply via uni-assist or the university's own portal. Deadlines vary by university, but many winter-semester deadlines fall between May and July and summer-semester deadlines often fall between November and January.

Will You Get a German Student Visa Without IELTS?

Yes, it is possible to get a German student visa without IELTS.

If your university clearly mentions in the admission letter that you meet the language requirements, the German embassy accepts this as valid proof.

In such cases, you do not need to submit IELTS or TOEFL during your visa appointment.

Important Visa Points to Remember

  • The admission letter must explicitly confirm language eligibility
  • MOI should be genuine and verifiable
  • Embassy decisions are based on university confirmation
  • Visa officers may still ask questions during the interview

A strong visa file, proper documentation, and clear academic intent play a crucial role in visa approval.

Documents Required for Masters in Germany Application

  • APS certificate (mandatory for all Indian students — see our APS certificate process)
  • Academic transcripts (10th, 12th, undergraduate — attested copies)
  • Degree certificate or provisional certificate
  • Medium of Instruction Certificate (if waiving IELTS)
  • Statement of Purpose (SOP)
  • 2–3 Letters of Recommendation (LOR)
  • CV / Resume (Europass format preferred)
  • Valid passport (must be valid through your program end date)
  • Portfolio (for design, architecture, or arts programs)

Once you have an admission letter, the next milestone is your Germany student visa requirements — including the blocked account, which is separate from the English-proficiency requirements covered in this guide.

Career Scope After Masters in Germany

Germany offers excellent career prospects after completing a master's degree, especially from public universities.

  • Engineering and IT roles in global companies
  • Research positions in universities and institutes
  • Opportunities in automotive, AI, renewable energy, and manufacturing
  • Start-up ecosystem in cities like Berlin and Munich
  • 18-month post-study job-search residence permit

A German master's degree is highly valued across Europe and internationally.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I do Masters in Germany without IELTS?
Yes. Many German universities waive the IELTS requirement for students who completed their undergraduate degree in English medium. You can submit a Medium of Instruction Certificate from your college as an alternative.

Which German universities accept Masters without IELTS?
Universities like TU Darmstadt, University of Freiburg, Freie Universität Berlin, and FAU Erlangen-Nuremberg have programs that waive the IELTS requirement for students with English-medium undergraduate degrees. Requirements vary by program.

What is accepted instead of IELTS for Germany Masters?
German universities that waive IELTS typically accept a Medium of Instruction Certificate, Duolingo English Test (DET score 110+), TOEFL (90+ iBT), or TestDaF for German-taught programs.

Is GRE required for Masters in Germany?
GRE is generally not required for Masters programs at German public universities. Most programs evaluate candidates on undergraduate GPA, language scores, SOP, and LORs.

Final Thoughts

Masters in Germany without IELTS is a realistic option in 2026 if you plan strategically.

By targeting universities that accept MOI and preparing your application carefully, you can study in Germany without standardized English tests and still secure a student visa.

title: How to Get Germany Student Visa Without Blocked Account: 4 Legal Alternatives (2026)
excerpt: Can you get a German student visa without a blocked account? Yes — but only with recognised alternatives. Learn all 4 legal options, who qualifies, embassy acceptance rates, and the real risks for Indian students in 2026.
content:
TL;DR: Yes, it's possible — but only if you qualify for a recognised alternative. This blog breaks down every legal option, who it works for, and the risks to watch out for.

Table of Contents

  1. What Is a Blocked Account and Why Does Germany Require It?
  2. The 2026 Blocked Account Amount
  3. Can You Skip It? The Honest Answer
  4. Alternative 1 — Scholarship Letter
  5. Alternative 2 — Verpflichtungserklärung (Sponsor Letter)
  6. Alternative 3 — Parental Bank Statements
  7. Alternative 4 — Bank Guarantee (Bankbürgschaft)
  8. Comparison Table — All Alternatives at a Glance
  9. FAQs Indian Students Always Ask

1. What Is a Blocked Account and Why Does Germany Require It?

A Blocked Account (Sperrkonto) is a special bank account that proves you can financially support yourself while studying in Germany — without relying on public funds or working illegally.

It's one of the most important documents in your visa application. Without it, or a valid alternative, your visa will almost certainly be rejected. If you're still finalising your admission, our Masters in Germany without IELTS guide covers the language-proficiency side of the application, separate from the financial proof covered here.

2. The 2026 Blocked Account Amount

The required deposit for 2026 is €11,904/year (€992/month). For the Chancenkarte (Opportunity Card), it's higher: €13,092/year (€1,091/month).

Note: this isn't a fee. Every euro is returned to you in monthly instalments while you study — it's your own money, just controlled.

3. Can You Skip It? The Honest Answer

Yes — but only in specific situations. Germany officially recognises four alternatives to the blocked account. Not all embassies accept all of them, and the blocked account remains the safest, most widely accepted route.

Important: rules vary between embassies and consulates. Always confirm with your specific one before relying on any alternative.

4. Alternative 1 — Scholarship Letter

A fully-funded scholarship from a recognised institution (DAAD, university, government-backed, or other recognised bodies) is one of the strongest alternatives.

Important: a partial scholarship doesn't fully replace the blocked account. If it covers only part of €11,904, you must top up the rest in a blocked account.

5. Alternative 2 — Verpflichtungserklärung (Sponsor Letter)

This is a legal declaration where someone already living in Germany guarantees to cover all your expenses during your stay. The sponsor must show sufficient income/assets and file the declaration with their local Ausländerbehörde.

Important: not accepted by all embassies. Some German consulates in India don't accept this as a standalone alternative — verify first.

6. Alternative 3 — Parental Bank Statements

Some embassies accept parents' bank statements as proof, but this is the least reliable alternative. It usually requires several months of statements plus a notarised declaration of support, and embassies are often sceptical of statements from certain countries due to fraud concerns.

Most consultants advise against relying on this alone — use it only as a supplementary document.

7. Alternative 4 — Bank Guarantee (Bankbürgschaft)

A Bankbürgschaft is a guarantee from a financial institution, where the bank promises to cover your obligations in Germany if you can't. It's costly, requires strong collateral, and isn't practical for most Indian students.

8. Comparison Table — All Alternatives at a Glance

  • Blocked Account: Universally accepted, ~€11,904 deposit, safest option
  • Scholarship Letter: Accepted if fully-funded and from a recognised body; partial scholarships need a top-up
  • Verpflichtungserklärung: Not accepted everywhere; needs a financially strong sponsor in Germany
  • Parental Bank Statements: Least reliable; use only as supporting evidence
  • Bank Guarantee: Rarely used; expensive and collateral-heavy

9. FAQs Indian Students Always Ask

Can Indian students get a German visa without a blocked account?Yes — but only with a recognised alternative like a full scholarship or a Verpflichtungserklärung. The blocked account remains the safest and most widely accepted option.

Which is the best blocked account provider for Indian students in 2026?Expatrio and Fintiba are the two most recommended providers. Expatrio charges a one-time fee of €49 and provides confirmation within 1–3 business days. Both are fully recognised by all German embassies.

What if I have a partial scholarship?A partial scholarship reduces the amount you need in your blocked account but does not replace it entirely. You must top up the remaining amount.

Is the blocked account money refundable if my visa is rejected?Yes. If your visa is rejected, your blocked account provider will return your money after deducting applicable fees.

How early should I open a blocked account?Open it as soon as you receive your university admission letter (Zulassungsbescheid). Processing takes 5–10 working days.

Can I use my Indian bank statement instead of a blocked account?No. Indian bank statements alone are not accepted as proof of funds for a German student visa.
